script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying David feels he owes the family a debt adds a feeling and motive the text does not give.
The princes accuse the servants of spying out and overthrowing the land, not necessarily taking over the whole country.
Saying Hanun acts on the princes' theory supplies a reason for his actions that the text does not state.
David's supposed reason for meeting the men before they walk very far is invented, even though marked as a guess. The text also does not say how quickly he acted.
Saying the Ammonites chose hired soldiers over making things right adds an alternative and a motive not given in the text.
Calling the hiring a way to avoid a conversation adds a motive the text does not give.
David sent the entire army of mighty men, not necessarily everyone.
The text does not say whether Joab panicked.
The text does not say Joab waited for nobody or specify exactly when and where he made the decision.
Joab arrayed men against the Arameans. The text does not say he personally took on the hired kings.
The comparison to a plan for anyone with a brother does not fit the action: Joab's plan is for two forces facing enemies in battle.
The text says the Arameans fled, but does not say how long they lasted.
Saying the Arameans ran instead of fighting adds a detail the text does not give.
Joab's worry, his reason for making the plan, and the claim that he did not need it are not stated in the text.
David gathered Israel, crossed the Jordan, and advanced, but the text does not say he was at the front.
Only one side being left standing goes beyond the text. It says the Arameans fled.
The text does not say Hadadezer's subjects never tried again.
The text says the Arameans were unwilling to help the Ammonites anymore, not that the silver deal was over.
The text does not say whether another attack was planned or establish that this was the end of their fighting.
The text says Hadadezer's subjects made peace, then says the Arameans were unwilling to help. It does not say all the Arameans made peace.
The text attributes making peace and becoming subject to Hadadezer's subjects, not all the Arameans. It also does not say the Ammonites had no other help.
The explanation is generic and ends with the flat observation that the crown is real treasure.
Saying this is the end of the crown suggests an outcome the text does not give.
The text does not say the crown changed heads for good.
The explanation is flat and repeats the placement of the crown without adding a distinctive Papa Dorin observation.
